about: Three maps of weather sites, for incident.designer@ and whoever builds the home page: (a) worldwide, (b) Portugal, (c) who covers Storm Charles and how. Kept by incident.weatherwatch@web-summit.dinis. Public sources only. This is research about how others present weather; it is not a forecast and not a warning service: warnings are IPMA's.
method: Each address was requested once from this session with a plain HTTP GET (no login, no script execution) between 23:38Z and 23:47Z on 10 November 2026. opened.status is the HTTP status; opened.read the UTC time; opened.seen says what the description rests on: "rendered" = also drawn in a headless browser at 23:48Z and looked at (opened.rendered.saw says what was seen; no image is kept); "html" = content read in the returned page; "json" = a data answer was read; "shell" = the page is drawn by script, only its shell and labels were read, and the description of the interactive part is general knowledge of the product, not an observation of this read; "blocked" = refused (401/403/429/bot check); "failed" = no answer or 404. Licence lines say "read" where the terms page was opened; otherwise they say so.

fields.how: tags: maps, warnings, timeline-hourly, presenter-video, radar, satellite, lightning, stations, models, tracker, liveblog, explainer, embed, interactive, feed, api, social
fields.data: api, licence, reuse (can we show its content: yes / with attribution / embed only / link only / no)
fields.learn: what our site should take from it
fields.rank: position within its map in the README ranking, where ranked

sites.name: Met Office (UK)
sites.shows: Home opens on the UK warnings map with a day strip (today and the next days, each coloured by its highest warning); a place search gives an hour-by-hour table (symbol, chance of rain, temperature, feels-like, wind and gust, visibility, humidity, UV). The UK Storm Centre lists the named storms of the season with the date named and the map of each; surface-pressure charts by forecaster.

data.api: Weather DataHub (site-specific, map images, atmospheric models); key needed; plans by daily request limit
data.licence: Crown copyright; website material under the UK Open Government Licence v3.0 unless marked; some data licensed for a fee
data.reuse: yes with attribution for OGL material

sites.best: The warnings page: one map, a day selector, and each warning written as "what to expect" in plain bullet points, with issued and updated times and a likelihood-by-impact matrix.
sites.learn: Write each warning as what to expect, not only as a colour; show the impact-likelihood matrix cell; one line "issued / updated" under every warning.

rendered.saw: UK warnings page with a day strip; "No warnings" for Tuesday 10 November, so the warning layout itself was not seen in use.

sites.name: US National Weather Service
sites.shows: A national hazards map coloured by warning type with a legend ordered by priority; each point forecast page has a "hazardous weather conditions" box first, then current conditions, a 7-day strip, an hourly graph (temperature, wind and gusts, precipitation chance as stacked charts) and the forecast discussion, the forecaster's own reasoning in text.

data.api: api.weather.gov: JSON-LD/GeoJSON, alerts in CAP, no key (a User-Agent is asked for)
data.licence: US government work: public domain (third-party imagery excepted)

sites.best: The forecast discussion: the reasoning and the uncertainty in the forecaster's words, timestamped, next to the numbers. And an open alerts API in a standard format (CAP).
sites.learn: Publish the reasoning beside the numbers, signed and timed; keep the hazards box above everything else on the page.

sites.name: US National Hurricane Center
sites.shows: One map of the basin with every active system; per storm a fixed set of products issued on a fixed clock (public advisory, forecast advisory, discussion, wind-speed probabilities) and the cone graphic: the track, the forecast points with times, the uncertainty cone, the coastal warnings.

data.api: RSS and GIS feeds (shapefile, KML) per storm; text products

sites.best: The fixed product set on a fixed clock: everyone knows when the next advisory comes and what will be in it. The cone states uncertainty in the picture itself.
sites.learn: Say when the next update is due (IPMA's next communiqué or warning revision), and draw uncertainty (the track "entering further south") rather than writing it only.

sites.name: Deutscher Wetterdienst (Germany)
sites.shows: Warnings map down to municipality level with a time slider; the WarnWetter app; a large open-data server (model output ICON, radar composites, station observations, warnings in CAP).

data.api: opendata.dwd.de: files over HTTPS, no key (GRIB, BUFR, CAP, CSV)
data.licence: CC BY 4.0 with source named (read on its legal notice)

sites.best: Open data at scale, including the model fields and the radar composite, under one plain licence.
sites.learn: A single plain licence line per dataset, as DWD does; ICON-EU fields are a reusable second model for Lisbon.

sites.name: Météo-France: Vigilance
sites.shows: The vigilance map: one colour per département, tabs for today and tomorrow, the issue time and the validity on the card, the time the next map is due, a legend written as actions, maps per phenomenon, and one bar per phenomenon along the hours of the day.

data.api: meteo.data.gouv.fr and a public API portal (key needed)
data.licence: French open licence (Etalab) for public data; not re-read in this pass

sites.best: The card says when it was issued, until when it is valid and when the next one comes; the legend is what to do, not what the colour is called.
sites.learn: Three times on the hero (issued, valid to, next due); a legend of actions in the authority's words; one bar per hazard along the day.

rendered.saw: One card: "Vigilance météorologique et crues", issued 10 November 16:00, valid to 12 November 00:00 (Paris time); two tabs, "Aujourd'hui" and "Demain" (the second greyed with "Prochaine carte à 06h": it says when the next map comes); the map by département in four colours with the legend as actions ("Soyez attentif", "Soyez très vigilant", "Vigilance absolue"); "cartes par phénomène" as a list; under the map one bar per phenomenon along the hours of the day (0h to 0h); and the line "updated at least twice a day, at 6h and 16h".

sites.name: AEMET (Spain)
sites.shows: Warnings map by zone with tabs for today, tomorrow and the day after and a table of every warning (zone, phenomenon, level, start, end, probability, comment). Keeps the season's list of high-impact storms named by the south-western group, with who named each and when, and a study of each episode afterwards.

data.licence: reuse allowed citing AEMET as the source, without distorting the information (read on its legal notice)

sites.best: The season table of named storms: name, type, date named, the service that named it, and a link to the episode study.
sites.learn: Our incident page should link the naming record; and promise the after-study ("estudio del episodio") as a section from the start.

opened.note: the 2026-2027 table lists Adam (16 Oct, AEMET) and Bruna (5 Nov, IPMA); the Charles row had no date or naming service filled in at 23:38Z

sites.name: Yr (MET Norway and NRK)
sites.owner: Norwegian Meteorological Institute and NRK (public broadcaster)
sites.shows: A place page with one table: a row per day that opens into a row per hour (symbol, temperature, precipitation in mm, wind speed with an arrow and the wind in words). The national service's warnings for the place sit above the table as banners that start with a status word (Ongoing, Expected), in English, worldwide: for Lisbon it showed IPMA's five warnings. Lisbon was read and rendered.

data.api: api.met.no (Locationforecast and others): JSON, no key, an identifying User-Agent required
data.licence: NLOD 2.0 and CC BY 4.0; credit MET Norway (read on its licence page)

sites.best: The calmest hour-by-hour table on the web, with the authority's warnings for that place above it, each with a status word. The same data is an open API for any point on Earth.
sites.learn: Warnings above the hours, each starting with Ongoing or Expected. And its flaw to avoid: automatic hourly wind of 4 to 10 m/s printed under a red wind warning with no word on why they differ.

opened.note: the help-centre page on terms returned 403; the API licence page was read instead

rendered.saw: Lisbon, hourly table for Wednesday 11 November: above the table, five warning banners for Lisboa in English, each starting with a status word ("Ongoing: Yellow Coastal Event Warning", "Expected: Orange Rain Warning", "Expected: Red Rain Warning", "Expected: Red Wind Warning", "Expected: Orange Coastal Event Warning"), each expandable; under them one row per hour: time, symbol, temperature, precipitation in mm, wind speed in m/s with an arrow, and the wind in words ("Fresh breeze from south east"). No gust column was shown. The automatic rows read 4 to 10 m/s for Lisbon under a banner carrying the red wind warning: the page does not comment on the difference.

sites.name: KNMI (Netherlands)
sites.shows: Home leads with the colour code for the country and a one-paragraph "weather picture" by the duty forecaster; KNMI Data Platform publishes observations, radar and HARMONIE model output.

data.api: KNMI Data Platform: Open Data API, EDR API, notification service (key needed)
data.licence: CC BY 4.0 on the datasets read

sites.best: The duty forecaster's short text on the home page, dated and plain.
sites.learn: A dated two-sentence "the picture now" by a named role, above the data.

sites.name: SMHI (Sweden)
sites.shows: Impact-based warnings (the same wind gets a different level by region and season), each with "what can happen"; open data API.

data.licence: CC BY 4.0 (not re-read in this pass)

sites.best: Warnings written from the consequences backwards.
sites.learn: Lead with the consequence ("trees down, roofs, power cuts"), then the number.

sites.name: Finnish Meteorological Institute
sites.shows: Local forecast with an hourly table and a 5-day warnings strip per region; open data (observations, radar, HARMONIE, lightning) also on a public cloud bucket.

data.api: WFS open data, no key for most
data.licence: CC BY 4.0 (read on its licence page)

sites.best: The warnings strip: five days across, one row per hazard.
sites.learn: A five-day strip with one row per hazard is the compact form of IPMA's warnings.

sites.name: Japan Meteorological Agency
sites.shows: One "disaster prevention" map application with every layer on the same base map (warnings, typhoon track and probability circle, rain nowcast, river flood and landslide risk meshes), in 15 languages; risk meshes are coloured by what to do, not by millimetres.

data.api: JSON behind the map, undocumented but stable; XML feeds
data.licence: government terms of use, compatible with CC BY (not re-read)

sites.best: Risk coloured by the action it asks for, on one map for every hazard.
sites.learn: One base map for everything; a legend that reads as actions.

sites.name: Bureau of Meteorology (Australia)
sites.shows: Redesigned home: a place card first (now, today, the next hours), then warnings for that place, then the radar; warnings list ordered by severity with issued times.

data.api: FTP/JSON products; reuse under its copyright notice
data.licence: CC BY for most Bureau material (not re-read)

sites.best: A page that starts from "your place, now" and puts warnings for that place directly under it.
sites.learn: Start from the reader's place (Lisbon by default), not from the country.

sites.name: Environment and Climate Change Canada
sites.shows: Alerts map and table; city pages with text forecast and hourly table; MSC Datamart and GeoMet open data.

data.api: MSC GeoMet (OGC API, WMS), Datamart; no key
data.licence: Environment and Climate Change Canada Data Servers End-use Licence (open, attribution)

sites.best: Open standards (OGC API) for every layer.
sites.learn: Serve our layers at stable, documented paths, as we do under api/v1.

sites.name: MeteoSwiss
sites.owner: Swiss Federal Office of Meteorology and Climatology
sites.shows: Home is the map with an animation bar (past radar into forecast, one continuous timeline); hazards by degree 1 to 5 with behaviour advice per degree.
sites.best: One time bar running from observed (radar) into forecast, the "now" line in the middle.
sites.learn: Our strip should run from observed gusts into the forecast with a clear "now" marker.

rendered.saw: Rendered, but only navigation text was captured; the time bar was not checked.

sites.name: Met Éireann (Ireland)
sites.shows: Warnings first on the home page as a list with status, validity and issue time; national forecast text by the forecaster; names storms with the western group.
sites.best: Warnings as text first: status, valid from/to, issued.
sites.learn: Every warning row carries valid-from, valid-to and issued.

sites.name: ECMWF charts and open data
sites.owner: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (intergovernmental)
sites.shows: The reference global model: chart catalogue (mean sea level pressure and wind, ensemble meteograms for any point, extreme forecast index). A subset of IFS and AIFS output is open data.

data.api: open data files (GRIB) and a client; charts via Open Charts
data.licence: CC BY 4.0 with the ECMWF Terms of Use: redistribution and commercial use allowed with attribution (read)

sites.best: The ensemble meteogram: the spread of 50 runs for one place as box-and-whisker by time step, uncertainty made visible. The extreme forecast index shows how unusual the forecast is for that place.
sites.learn: Show a spread, not one line, for Lisbon's gusts where we have several models; say how unusual a value is for the place.

opened.note: charts.ecmwf.int answered with a bot check; the open-data and licence pages were read

sites.name: EUMETSAT EUMETView
sites.shows: Satellite imagery viewer (Meteosat: airmass, natural colour, infrared) with animation; OGC services (WMS/WMTS).

data.licence: EUMETSAT data policy: most Meteosat imagery free with attribution; the licensing page was a script shell here
data.reuse: yes with attribution (to confirm per product)

sites.best: The airmass composite: the one image that shows a deepening Atlantic low and its dry intrusion.
sites.learn: One satellite frame with its time, linked to the source, says "where is it now" better than text; pointer only, no image in git.

sites.name: MeteoAlarm
sites.owner: EUMETNET (the network of European national services)
sites.shows: One map of Europe coloured by the highest warning per region, from the national services themselves; per country a list with level, hazard, validity; Atom/CAP feeds per country. Portugal's feed was read: 122 entries at 23:35Z, levels Moderate, Severe and Extreme.

data.api: Atom + CAP feeds per country, no key
data.licence: terms equivalent to CC BY 4.0 with extra conditions for redistribution (read in the feed)
data.reuse: yes with attribution and its conditions

sites.best: The same colours and the same format for every country: IPMA and AEMET on one map, machine-readable in CAP.
sites.learn: Show Spain's warnings beside Portugal's from one feed; keep the four European colours exactly.

rendered.saw: Portugal: a map coloured by district (Madeira red; the mainland yellow and orange at 23:00 to 02:00), a time bar with buttons Now, +24h and each day to Saturday plus "Animation", filters by awareness level and hazard type, and a list of areas, one row per warning with the hazard pictogram on its colour.

sites.name: WMO Severe Weather Information Centre
sites.shows: World map of official warnings and tropical cyclones from national services, in CAP.

data.api: CAP feeds via the WMO Alert Hub

sites.best: Only official sources, worldwide.
sites.learn: The rule we already follow: the authority's warning, never ours.

sites.name: Copernicus Emergency Management Service
sites.shows: Rapid mapping activations (satellite damage and flood extent maps) and EFAS flood forecasts.
sites.best: After the event: the mapped extent, with its provenance.
sites.learn: Watch for an activation for Portugal after the storm; none named Charles was listed at 23:40Z.

sites.name: NASA Worldview / GIBS
sites.shows: Daily global true-colour imagery with a date slider; GIBS serves the tiles.
sites.best: A date slider over imagery: yesterday against today.
sites.learn: A before/after slider is the form for the day after.

sites.name: BBC Weather
sites.owner: BBC (public broadcaster); forecast data from a commercial provider
sites.shows: A place page that is one horizontal strip: day tabs across the top, under them an hour-by-hour row (symbol, temperature, chance of precipitation, wind arrow with speed; tap an hour for gust, humidity, pressure, visibility); warnings as a labelled bar above the strip; a presenter video forecast and a one-sentence text summary for the day. Lisbon was read.

data.licence: BBC terms: no reuse without permission; link and short quotation only

sites.best: The hour strip with the sentence above it: "what kind of day" in words, then every hour in one scrollable line, on a phone. The presenter video is the same forecast told by a person.
sites.learn: The hero: one sentence, then the hour strip; a named voice ("the presenter") is a text block with a time and a role, not a video.

rendered.saw: Lisbon: a card "Tonight" with one sentence ("Thundery showers and a gentle breeze"), day tabs for eight days with high and low, an hour row (symbol, temperature, chance of precipitation, a wind circle with speed), "Last updated today at 23:02", then a rain map with a play button and a week-long time bar. No warning of any kind was shown for Lisbon on the eve of IPMA's red warnings: outside the UK the page carries no authority's warnings.

sites.name: The Weather Channel (weather.com)
sites.shows: Place card (now, feels like, high/low), hourly and 10-day, radar map, video; alerts as a red bar at the very top.
sites.best: The alert bar: one line, the highest alert, always at the top.
sites.learn: One persistent line at the top with the highest current warning and its end time.

sites.name: AccuWeather
sites.shows: Not opened (403). Known for minute-by-minute precipitation and its own impact scales.
sites.best: Not assessed.
sites.learn: Not assessed.

sites.name: meteoblue
sites.shows: Lisbon read: a 7-day strip with predictability per day as a percentage; meteograms; the multi-model diagram (every model's line for one place on one chart) and a "where are the clouds now" map.

data.licence: all rights reserved; attribution required for the free tier

sites.best: A predictability figure per day and the multi-model chart: disagreement between models shown, not hidden.
sites.learn: Put a confidence note on each day; when two models disagree on the peak hour, show both.

sites.name: Weather Underground
sites.shows: A network of personal weather stations on a map (Lisbon has many), each with its own page and history graph.
sites.best: Density: a reading from the next street.
sites.learn: Amateur stations are evidence, labelled as such, never fact.

sites.name: Foreca
sites.shows: Clean place pages, hourly table, rain radar.
sites.best: Plain hourly layout.
sites.learn: Nothing beyond Yr.

sites.name: Weather & Radar
sites.shows: Radar-first home page with a play bar from past to forecast.
sites.best: Radar as the first thing seen.
sites.learn: For a rain event the radar is the hero; for wind it is the gust strip.

sites.name: Windy
sites.shows: A full-screen animated map (wind particles over a colour field) with a layer menu (wind, gusts, rain, waves, pressure), a model switch (ECMWF, GFS, ICON, AROME) and a time slider along the bottom; click a point for a forecast table that compares models; radar, satellite, webcams and station reports as layers. Embeddable as an iframe with a chosen place, layer and model.

data.api: paid Point Forecast and Map Forecast APIs; free embed widget (iframe)
data.licence: all rights reserved; embed allowed as provided

sites.best: The model switch on the same map and the same hour: the fastest way to see whether models agree on where the low goes.
sites.learn: If we show a moving map, embed it with its credit rather than copy it; keep it below the fold, since it loads slowly and says nothing about decisions.

rendered.saw: The gust layer over Portugal rendered as a full-screen map with place labels; no text about warnings.

sites.name: Ventusky
sites.shows: Animated map like Windy, with a strong gust layer and fronts drawn on the map; embeddable. Observador embeds it (gust layer, two models) in its Charles special.
sites.best: Gusts and fronts on one map.
sites.learn: The press already uses this embed; two embeds with two models side by side is Observador's way to show uncertainty.

sites.name: earth.nullschool.net
sites.shows: The globe with flowing wind lines (GFS), minimal chrome: the picture is the page.

data.licence: all rights reserved (the original code is MIT on GitHub)

sites.best: Beauty and legibility of a single field.
sites.learn: One field, no chrome: restraint.

sites.name: Zoom Earth
sites.shows: Near-real-time satellite imagery with a time scrubber; radar, wind and pressure layers; tropical storm tracks with forecast cone.

data.licence: all rights reserved; imagery from public agencies

sites.best: The scrubber: drag time over real satellite imagery.
sites.learn: A time scrubber is the interaction people understand; ours scrubs the hour strip.

opened.note: no page for Charles (it tracks tropical systems)

sites.name: Open-Meteo
sites.shows: A free JSON API over the open models of the national services (ECMWF, DWD ICON, Météo-France AROME/ARPEGE, and others), hourly, any point, with gusts; an ensemble API and a historical API. A call for Lisbon (hourly gusts and precipitation, two days) answered in 534 bytes.

data.api: HTTP GET, no key, no sign-up
data.licence: CC BY 4.0 for the data; the free tier is for non-commercial use

sites.best: Several models for one place in one call, with a clear licence.
sites.learn: The source for a model-spread strip for Lisbon (labelled analysis material, never a warning).

sites.name: Pirate Weather
sites.shows: An open forecast API in the old Dark Sky shape (minutely, hourly, alerts).
sites.best: Minutely precipitation in an open API.
sites.learn: None for Lisbon beyond Open-Meteo.

sites.name: RainViewer
sites.shows: Worldwide radar composite as map tiles with past frames.

data.licence: free for personal, educational and small community use only (read on its API page)

sites.best: Radar tiles anyone can put on a map.
sites.learn: Possible radar layer; check the terms fit a public newsroom first.

sites.name: Blitzortung / LightningMaps
sites.shows: Real-time lightning strikes on a map, from volunteers' receivers.

data.licence: non-commercial; raw data only for participants (read)

sites.best: Seconds-old data from a citizen network.
sites.learn: Link, do not copy; IPMA has its own lightning page.

sites.name: Meteociel
sites.shows: Every model run as static charts (GFS, ECMWF, AROME, ARPEGE, ICON), observations and soundings; dense, fast, old-fashioned.
sites.best: Speed and completeness: every run, every field, no script.
sites.learn: Fast static pages beat pretty slow ones during an incident.

sites.name: Wetterzentrale
sites.shows: Model chart archive and ensembles ("spaghetti" plots).
sites.best: Ensemble plots for a point.
sites.learn: As ECMWF: spread over single line.

sites.name: Tropical Tidbits
sites.shows: Model charts with a frame slider and keyboard stepping; storm pages.
sites.best: Keyboard stepping through time.
sites.learn: Arrow keys step our hour strip.

sites.name: Windguru
sites.shows: A colour-coded table for a spot (Guincho was read and rendered): live readings from nearby stations first, then columns of hours and rows for wind, gust, direction, wave, period, rain; cell colour is the value; one table per model with its run time.
sites.best: The heat-map table: forty hours of six variables readable at a glance.
sites.learn: Colour the cells of our hour strip by threshold (IPMA's yellow/orange/red gust criteria).

rendered.saw: Guincho: a "Live Wind" strip of nearby stations with their current reading first (Cabo Raso, Cascais), then the table: columns every two hours for a week, rows for wind speed, gusts, direction, wave, period, temperature, cloud, rain, every cell coloured by its value; the same table repeated per model below, with the model run time ("init") on each.

sites.name: Windfinder
sites.shows: Wind map and spot forecasts with live station reports.
sites.best: Measured against forecast at the same spot.
sites.learn: We already plot observed gusts against forecast: keep it on the home page.

sites.name: ESTOFEX
sites.shows: Convective outlooks for Europe: a map with level lines and a reasoned text.
sites.best: A reasoned outlook, signed.
sites.learn: For tornado or squall-line risk it is evidence from experts, labelled.

sites.name: European Severe Weather Database
sites.shows: Quality-controlled reports of severe weather events (wind, tornado, hail, rain) on a map.
sites.best: Each report has a quality level.
sites.learn: Our evidence items could carry a quality level the same way.

sites.name: Severe Weather Europe
sites.shows: Long explainers on large events with many model charts.
sites.best: Depth for enthusiasts.
sites.learn: Nothing on Charles on its front page at 23:40Z.

sites.name: FU Berlin: Aktion Wetterpate
sites.shows: Names every low and high over Europe (a second, older naming scheme); daily analysis charts with the names.
sites.best: A second name for the same low: useful for searching German-language coverage.
sites.learn: Record other names for the same storm in incident.json.

sites.name: Iowa Environmental Mesonet
sites.shows: Archive of METAR/TAF worldwide and of every US warning text, with download.
sites.best: History of every airport report.
sites.learn: Lisbon airport's past METARs for the after-study.

sites.name: Aviation Weather Center data API
sites.shows: METAR and TAF for any airport as JSON; Lisbon's TAF answered.
sites.best: The airport forecast as data.
sites.learn: Already used by the meteorologist for the airport.

sites.name: OGIMET
sites.shows: Decoded SYNOP, METAR and TAF archive for any station.
sites.best: Raw reports nobody else keeps public.
sites.learn: Backup source for station gusts.

sites.name: Kachelmannwetter / meteologix / weather.us
sites.shows: Not opened: refused our request (bot check).
sites.best: Not assessed.
sites.learn: Not assessed.

sites.name: WXCharts
sites.shows: Not opened: refused our request (bot check).
sites.best: Not assessed.
sites.learn: Not assessed.

sites.name: Netweather
sites.shows: Not opened: refused our request (bot check).
sites.best: Not assessed.
sites.learn: Not assessed.

sites.name: Pivotal Weather
sites.shows: Not opened: refused our request (bot check).
sites.best: Not assessed.
sites.learn: Not assessed.

sites.name: IPMA
sites.owner: Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera (the State's meteorological authority)
sites.shows: Home: the map of warnings by district with a day selector, the forecast for the capitals, the latest communiqués and the seismic map. The authority for every warning in Portugal and the service that named Charles.

data.api: api.ipma.pt open data: JSON, no key (warnings up to 3 days, daily forecast by city, hourly station observations, sea state, seismic events)
data.licence: use allowed for personal or public purposes that are not for profit or offensive, always naming the source (read on api.ipma.pt)

sites.best: It is the primary source: the warning itself, the communiqué itself, with validity times.
sites.learn: Everything in our hero comes from here and links here; our job is to make its content faster to read, not to add to it.

rendered.saw: Home (updated 2026/11/10 23:31 UTC): tabs "Hoje", "Amanhã", "Depois de Amanhã", each with a warning triangle in the day's highest colour (red, red, yellow); the daily forecast map; the warnings map (mainland, Azores, Madeira); a "Comunicados" box; yesterday's extremes by station; small tiles for model charts, satellite, seismic activity.

sites.name: IPMA: warnings on a timeline
sites.shows: "Avisos meteorológicos em linha temporal": for a district, one row per hazard and coloured bars along a three-day time axis (yellow, orange, red), with the text of each warning. The JSON behind it is api.ipma.pt/open-data/forecast/warnings/warnings_www.json.
sites.best: The Gantt of warnings: when each hazard starts and ends, in one picture.
sites.learn: This is the model for our strip: hazards as rows, hours as columns, IPMA's colours; add the events we track (Web Summit day, transport) as extra rows.

opened.note: the chart is drawn by script; the JSON was read

rendered.saw: Lisboa, last update 10 November 21:23 UTC: eight hazard rows (thunder, sea state, rain, wind, snow, cold, heat, fog) by 72 hourly cells for 11, 12 and 13 November, coloured green, yellow, orange, red; under it each warning as a coloured bar with hazard, level, start and end and one line of text, e.g. "Vento - Vermelho [11 Nov 12:00 - 11 Nov 21:00]: Rajadas até 120 km/h, podendo atingir 140 km/h nos locais mais expostos" and "Precipitação - Vermelho [11 Nov 09:00 - 11 Nov 18:00]"; a district list on the right with each district's highest level; "Toda a informação em horas UTC".

sites.name: IPMA: communiqués
sites.shows: Special information notes. Read at 23:40Z: communiqué no. 2 on Charles, "Chuva, vento e agitação marítima - Depressão CHARLES - Continente e Madeira", valid from 2026-11-10 17:07 to 2026-11-11 23:59, stating that CHARLES is the name IPMA gave the low and where it is forecast to be centred at 00 UTC on 11 November. An RSS feed carries each communiqué.

data.licence: as IPMA; its notice says copyright does not apply to communiqués

sites.best: The forecaster's own account of the storm, numbered and with a validity window.

sites.name: IPMA: forecast by place, hourly
sites.shows: Ten days for a place: day tabs carrying each day's warning colour, then one column per hour with rows for symbol, rain probability, temperature, mean wind, sea state and, last, the warnings as one coloured cell per hour.

data.api: daily by city in the open API; the hourly series is on the site

sites.best: The warnings as a row of the hourly table itself: hazard level and hour on one axis with the weather.
sites.learn: The model for our strip, with one change: put the warnings row first, not last, and label the automatic rows as automatic, since they read far below the warning's gusts (IPMA says so only in the notes).

rendered.saw: Lisboa (updated 2026-11-10 19:56:03 UTC): ten day tabs, each with symbol, min and max, wind, rain probability and the day's warning colour as a label ("Amarelo", "Vermelho", "Amarelo"); under them one column per hour of Wednesday 11 with rows: symbol, probability of precipitation, temperature and felt temperature, mean wind in km/h with direction, sea state (height, direction, water temperature) and a last row, "Avisos Meteorológicos", one coloured cell per hour (yellow, then orange, then red from 09H to 21H). The mean wind row reads 11 to 23 km/h under the red cells; the page explains in its notes that this automatic forecast may differ from the forecasters' descriptive forecast and warnings, which should be consulted.

sites.name: Renascença: "Monitorização Depressão Charles"
sites.shows: The only purpose-built tracker found. A dashboard with two views: weather warnings (a risk map by warning area, a national severity figure, "warnings in my area" by the reader's location, the day's warnings sorted by importance and time) and civil-protection occurrences (a map with markers coloured by state: under way, being resolved, concluding, dispatched; a number on a marker when several share a place; a filter by state). Built with an open map library; data loaded by script.
sites.best: Warnings and occurrences in one tool, with "my area" and occurrence states.
sites.learn: The closest thing to our site. It has no timeline, no decisions, no sources per item and no machine-readable twin: those are ours. Its occurrence-state legend and "my area" are worth matching.
